title: The Editorial Page of the Wall Street Journal Degrades Itself

content_html_sanitized:
MarijuanaNews note: As a “matter of policy” I try to stay “on topic”, to focus on marijuana prohibition, even avoiding the larger Drug War, etc. At the same time, I want to be candid about my views, which is especially appropriate in the present context. In this case, it is easy because I actually believe in the credo below that the WSJ editorial board falsely claims to believe. I have read the Journal since before most of their writers were born, and many of our fellow Conservatives, who were once Prohibionists, have changed their views, but not the WSJ.

 

My favorite economists are Ludwig von Mises, Frederick Hayek, and Milton Friedman, all anti Prohibitionists.

 

Friedman actually wrote an Oped for the WSJ, calling for the legalization of marijuana. He was ignored, and the Journal followed whoever told them what they wanted to hear.

 

In the present case, they have engaged in an extraordinary act of intellectual self degradation according to their professed principles below.

From the Editorial Page of the Wall Street Journal

The Editorial Board speaks for free markets and free people, the principles, if you will, marked in the watershed year of 1776 by Thomas Jefferson's Declaration of Independence and Adam Smith's “Wealth of Nations.” So over the past century and into the next, the Journal stands for free trade and sound money; against confiscatory taxation and the ukases of kings and other collectivists; and for individual autonomy against dictators, bullies and even the tempers of momentary majorities.”

 

As it happens, I wrote about the same story on Tuesday. Frankly, I was being lazy. It is intellectually pathetic, so I should thank the WSJ for redeeming my Tuesday.

See

Marijuana Prohibition and The Prostitution of Science

 

More Marijuana Users Are Crash Dummies

High-on-pot drivers are contributing to more highway accident deaths.

The Editorial Board

Oct. 8, 2025

Marijuananews note: They did not provide a link to the study.

 

How much social and public-health damage will Americans suffer before doing a U-turn on marijuana promotion?

Marijuananews note: Legalization equals “promotion”? Legalization is promotion of alcohol, adultery, blasphemy, divorce, charging interest on loans? All have been illegal at some point in the past.

 

Researchers from Wright State University analyzed driver autopsy results from car crashes in Montgomery County, Ohio, between January 2019 and September 2024. More than four in 10 tested positive for pot’s psychoactive ingredient THC, with an average level of 30.7 nanograms. That’s more than six times the level most states use to define impairment.

 

Breathalyzers won’t detect recent marijuana use, which makes it hard for police to nab people who are driving while high. Today’s marijuana is five times more potent than the weed that Boomers smoked when they were younger, so it takes less to become impaired.

 

Auto fatalities have increased over the last decade even as cars have become safer and alcohol consumption has fallen. Could marijuana be contributing to more reckless driving? It’s a fair question. Nearly a quarter of 18- to 25-year-olds used marijuana in the last month, according to a federal survey. As did 15% of those 26 or older.

Marijuananews note: Oddly, the Journal editorial mentions alcohol, which the report did not, which is rather absurd in this context, because alcohol is the leading cause of traffic fatalities, but also the largest cause of avoidable deaths in America. Is it there intention to give the impression that cannabis was the sole of the accidents.

 

The Ohio study, which is being presented this week at an American College of Surgeons conference, ought to prompt the Trump Administration to slam the brakes on a mooted plan to move marijuana to a less risky level on the federal drug schedule. Such a move would cultivate the spurious belief that marijuana isn’t all that harmful despite reams of evidence to the contrary.

Marijuananews note: How pathetically ignorant or appallingly dishonest. The proposed rescheduling has nothing to do with “risk.”

Schedule 1 is for drugs that have NO MEDICAL USE. Are the editors of the Journal really opposed to the medical use of cannabis???

If so, at least say so!

 

Moving it to Schedule 2 would keep the tax penalties and put it in the same risk category with Fentanyl, which is absurd. So this is the only instance where the WSJ is in favor of “confiscatory taxation.”

See

Marijuana Is In Schedule One. Fentanyl Is In Schedule 2. Think About It.

 

If your sole motivation is to raise taxes on marijuana businesses this is a messy way to do it. At no point here do they seem to understand the scheduling process or what is being proposed. Schedule one drugs supposedly have no recognized medical use.

 

Of course, the marijuana reform movement and medical marijuana patients have not been blocking the research and have never had the ability to do so.

 

Marijuana can damage the heart, lungs, immune system and brain. A study this spring in the Journal of the American College of Cardiology found that marijuana users under age 50 who were free of cardiovascular disease were six times as likely to suffer a heart attack compared to non-users and were at four-fold increased risk of stroke.

 

Have we gone from concern about traffic risks to internal medicine? Correlation is not causation. But, should alcohol and tobacco be illegal? Where is Al Capone when we really need him?

 

From the Centers for Disease Control: “Excessive alcohol use is a leading preventable cause of death in the United States. About 178,000 people die from excessive drinking each year.” They do not report any immediately-related marijuana deaths.

 

Americans were told that legalizing marijuana would reduce the illegal market, but that hasn’t happened.

 

Actually, it has. Approximately, 30% of the cannabis supply is in the legal industry. Recreational cannabis is still illegal in half the states, and no one claimed that legalization in some states would end the black market everywhere. As a business journal they should know better.

 

Moreover, had the WSJ chosen to follow its professed principles it would have rightly criticized the overtaxation, and excessive regulation that has hampered the industry. Instead, they act as though the persistence of the black market is somehow the fault of the overtaxed and over regulated industry. One would think that a business journal would know better.

 

California officials last month said they destroyed more than 20,000 illegal cannabis plants at operations run by transnational criminal organizations. They also found firearms and hazardous pesticides that contaminate the environment.

 

Illegal firearms in America! We never had that problem until those damn trigger happy hippies started smoking weed!

 

When criminals steal or destroy the natural resources that support California’s extraordinary biodiversity, we are committed to stopping them,” said a state wildlife official. Wouldn’t it be nice if progressives warned pot users about doing damage to themselves? What the country needs is a group called Mothers Against Drugged Drivers.

 

Oh, we have something better than that! It’s called the DEA, and there have been over 30 million arrests (roughly 85% for simple possession) since Nixon escalated the war on weed, and it continues at the rate of one every two minutes.

See How Many Americans Will Be Arrested While You Are Reading This Article?

Does the Journal oppose this?

 

But the whole point of this editorial is undermined by the following “findings”

● “No Effect from Legalization: The rate of drivers who tested positive for THC did not change significantly before or after legalization (42.1% vs. 45.2%), indicating that legal status did not influence the behavior of those who chose to drive after use.

● Consistent Over Time: The high rate of THC positivity showed no significant change over the six-year study period.”

In other words, the whole editorial is based on a false premise, denouncing something that was not in the report, which is even more pathetic.

 

Also, the cohort (young men) that has the most traffic accidents (and fatalities) is also the group that use the most cannabis, so some correlation is to be expected. Also, alcoholics use more cannabis than the average person. So, there may be a serious problem here, but the WSJ editorial page is not to be taken seriously, except as a threat to our freedom. Of course, their whole editorial page is based on principles that they don’t believe.

Why People Who Hate Cannabis And/Or Think It Is Dangerous Should Be Opposed To Prohibition
